parsed.explanation: No criminalisation of trans expression, no documented facility or birth-sex rule, no border/document friction, no police targeting, and no universal-exposure measure — and the dossier is legally well-documented, so that silence carries weight. Courts have granted gender-marker recognition (2017/2022) and LGBTI organisations can register; employment protection now names gender identity; constitutional 'any other status' is read to cover it — a functioning rule-of-law trajectory with active civil society. Offsetting this: enforcement and social conditions lag, with a UN submission recording daily discrimination, violence and stigmatisation for LGBTI people (not trans-specific or visitor-scoped, so moderate weight), hate-speech provisions expressly cover only sexual orientation, and no visitor-facing service remedy is demonstrated. Worst documented tier is societal hostility with some recourse (tier 3), not a tier-1 state exposure. This sits in the reduced-risk band with real but nontrivial friction.
